   STAFF REPORT

 Meeting Date:  April 6, 2026

 To:  Community Security Ad Hoc Liaisons Honorable Mayor Nazarian
  & Councilmember Friedman

 From:  Joana Torres, Community Services Manager
  Stephanie Harris, Director of Community Services

 Subject:  Safety and Hospitality Services

 Attachment:  None

INTRODUCTION
Staff is returning to the Community Security Ad Hoc for consideration of alternative options
for service delivery prior to the expiration of the current agreement for Ambassador
services, which concludes on June 30, 2026, unless extended or a new agreement is
executed.

Upon completing a Request for Proposal process and several interviews with staff and the
Liaisons, at the City Council Meeting of October 10, 2024 the City Council approved the
Ad Hoc’s short-term recommendation to extend Block by Block’s (BBB) services. The
recommended extended services are under a shorter-term agreement, concluding in June
30, 2026, with a reduced scope of services to allow the Ad Hoc time to explore and
recommend alternative methods of service delivery.

The origin of this short-term agreement began in 2024, when the Community Security Ad
Hoc, then composed of Mayor Friedman and Councilmember Corman, proposed a new
scope of work for Safety and Hospitality Services along with consolidation of services,
reduction of routes, and consolidation of shifts. This included consolidation of overnight
security functions and parking garage checks with current public safety contractor, as they
are more integrated with BHPD for security services and engaged throughout the City.

There was also a recommendation to reduce the footprint for hospitality services.
Hospitality services in the Business Triangle and South Beverly Drive would maintain
current service levels, while reducing Ambassador coverage outside of these areas.
Lastly, the Ad Hoc recommended a reduction in the hours of service and number of shifts
provided by Ambassadors to better align with the peak visitor hours.

DISCUSSION
Community Security Ad Hoc members, Mayor Nazarian and Councilmember Friedman
met on January 6, 2026, to discuss the impacts of the reduced services to the business
triangle. While it was agreed that there is a positive response to the service, it was agreed
 Meeting Date: April 6, 2026
that a hospitality approach was no longer necessary and perhaps the service should move
to enforcement. The Ad Hoc requested staff to consult the Rodeo Drive Committee and
the Chamber of Commerce.
After informal discussions with City partners, community feedback generally supports the
concept of maintaining a presence in these areas; however, it generally supported a focus
on engagements related to homeless outreach and code enforcement. The feedback did
not indicate a full-scale security deployment. It favored a ‘softer’ approach than the tactical
look of armed security and would be a ‘step-up’ from the current uniform appearance. The
feedback supported the continued efforts to engage unhoused individuals with the goal of
providing needed services and documentation of these ongoing efforts.
Additionally, there is a desire to see more engagement in the form of outreach, education
and documentation of those engaging in code enforcement violations, including non-
permitted commercial activities. In all cases, in the presence of ongoing or repetitive
violations, a process that supports more consistent and effective enforcement is favored
when outreach, education and assistance fails to remedy the violations.
Based on the ongoing input from the Ad Hoc and feedback from the Community, staff
suggests a 1 to 2 year pilot program utilizing the City’s current security services provider
as an alternative method of service delivery. Staff would work with the current provider to
scope a new mission, which will support outreach, engagement and education to
encourage acceptance of services and/or reducing violations. These services will also
focus on more direct engagement and documentation of ongoing and repetitive violations
for the escalation of services, such as with mental health concerns or the potential future
enforcement of code violations.

FISCAL IMPACT
No fiscal impact at this time.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff will bring forward the Ad Hoc’s recommendation to the full City Council for approval.

  Stephanie Harris,
  Director of Community Services
  Approved By
